title: Health crisis brews at Delhi protest as heat & overcrowding trigger viral infections
content: Protesters at Jantar Mantar are experiencing viral infections and dehydration. Volunteer doctors are treating many individuals for sore throats and fevers. Overcrowding and open sleeping conditions are worsening the health situation for attendees. Elderly protesters are also seeking care for existing conditions like diabetes and hypertension. Injuries from police action and general fatigue are also being addressed by medical volunteers.

title: Why IOC won't investigate Infantino over Trump's role in Balogun red-card controversy
content: The International Olympic Committee will not investigate FIFA president Gianni Infantino.  This decision stems from a complaint regarding Folarin Balogun's World Cup suspension reversal.  The IOC stated it lacks jurisdiction over FIFA's internal governance matters.  Norway's Football Federation will consider filing its own ethics complaint against Infantino.  FIFA has not yet commented on the ethics complaints or its decision.

title: 'Have a heart': Sonam Wangchuk's wife slams critics after he ends 26-day hunger strike
content: Gitanjali Angmo defended her husband Sonam Wangchuk's hunger strike conclusion.  He ended his 26-day fast after prolonged negotiations with Union ministers.  Wangchuk stated the decision aimed to prevent potential violence across the nation.  Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party vows to continue its peaceful protests.  They demand the education minister's resignation over the alleged NEET paper leak.

title: US to top universities: Scientists can 'help' America beat China more than you
content: The US government plans to fund individual scientists directly, moving away from large institutions. This strategic shift aims to accelerate technological discovery and maintain American leadership in science. Federal agencies are tasked with submitting action plans within ninety days for implementation. The report emphasizes revitalizing science and technology through AI and new research organizations. This initiative seeks to ensure scientific advancements benefit all Americans across the nation.

title: Why world is coming to India for medical treatment — and not just because it is cheaper
content: India's medical tourism market is experiencing significant growth, projected to reach $16.2 billion by 2030. Patients are increasingly choosing India for its affordable and high-quality medical treatments. Digital advancements and government initiatives are further enhancing the medical travel ecosystem. International patients praise the convenience, speed, and professional care received in India. Continued collaboration will solidify India's position as a global medical destination.

title: Nokia once sold 2 in 5 phones on Earth, then lost it all in 7 years
content: With its groundbreaking products, Nokia ruled the global mobile market for years, driven by efficient industrial logistics and far-reaching distribution. However, internal anxiety and limited communication led to several missteps. The arrival of the iPhone and Android revolutionized the landscape, shifting attention to software ecosystems. Ultimately, Nokia's mobile phone business was acquired by Microsoft, marking a pivotal change in its trajectory.

title: Oregon may charge tech firms for undersea cables to fund public schools
content: Oregon is introducing new fees for undersea cable installations near its coast.  These charges will generate revenue for the state's public K-12 schools.  Existing fees were established about twenty-five years ago and were much lower.  The new rates aim to attract tech investment while ensuring compensation.  This update follows a 2020 incident involving a cable construction project.

title: NY mayor hires Lina Khan who went after Amazon, Meta and Google in her days as FTC head

The former chair of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) known for her aggressive antitrust lawsuits against Big Tech. According to Business Insider, Mamdani called the duo a “dream team” and framed the appointments as a strategic effort to pair urban business growth with his progressive affordability agenda.

title: Centre suggests accelerated implementation to curb pollution in a time-bound manner
content: The Centre reviewed Haryana's air pollution control measures and urged faster implementation. Focus is on stubble burning, industrial pollution, and road dust reduction. Efforts will accelerate EV adoption and manage legacy waste effectively. Information campaigns and farmer training will promote crop residue management. Strict enforcement and coordination are critical for cleaner air.

title: The Odyssey beats Oppenheimer with director’s biggest opening weekend
content: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is showing no signs of slowing down at the global box office. The epic action-adventure has earned an estimated $346 million worldwide in its first week, making it Christopher Nolan's biggest box office opening ever and one of the highest-grossing films of 2026. Made on a reported $250 million budget, the adaptation of Homer's epic poem recovered its production cost within just three days of release.

title: Amid rain & fresh landslides, Jammu-Srinagar NH closure enters Day 3

Major pilgrimages, including Amarnath and Vaishno Devi Yatras, are suspended for the sixth consecutive day. Several vehicles are stranded as authorities advise against travel due to safety concerns. Flash floods also affected households in Udhampur district without any casualties.

title: How Serena Williams overcame poverty to become a tennis icon
content: Serena Williams grew up in a family that struggled financially but never gave up on their dream. Guided by her parents, Richard Williams and Oracene Price, she trained on public courts with limited resources before becoming one of tennis' greatest champions. Her journey from humble beginnings to 23 Grand Slam singles titles remains an inspiring story of resilience, sacrifice and unwavering family support.

title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes turned family pain into a heartfelt mission
content: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes attended a back-to-school event with FARE just before Chiefs training camp, continuing their advocacy for food allergy awareness. The couple's mission comes from personal experience after their children, Sterling and Bronze, were diagnosed with food allergies. Brittany has previously shared the frightening details of Bronze's severe allergic reaction and how it inspired the family to help others. Here's how Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes are using their platform to support parents and create safer environments for children with food allergies.
